name: Support ticket triage
summary: Your queue manager opens the morning’s tickets already sorted: each one with a category, a priority and a route, and the reason for all three in a line. The tickets that cannot wait sit at the top, stopped for a person to decide.

sources.title: Its own working guide for triage from a queue export against a team's written rules.

sources.contribution: The order of the triage work: read the whole ticket, categorize by cause, set a priority from impact and urgency, check for duplicates and known issues, then route with a reason. The invented rule set in the worked example is modelled on this source's category list, its four-level priority ladder (P1 to P4) and its first-reply targets (1 hour, 4 hours, 1 working day, 2 working days), and on its frontline, senior, billing and product routes.

The idea that some tickets leave ordinary support on stated conditions (security, breadth, a customer at risk, a pattern across tickets) and that the person receiving one needs who is affected, since when, what is known and what is not. The worked example's rules that raise a ticket past its reply target and treat the same fault in three or more tickets as a pattern follow this source's triggers.
